session.question: How do the themes of "Environmental sustainability", "Sustainability implementation barriers", and "Sustainable residential buildings" connect when comparing off-site construction research with the barrier analysis in Ghana and the "Mostadam" approach in Saudi Arabia, and what sustainability-related findings are highlighted across these contexts?
session.answer:
The three themes connect through a common focus on making residential construction more environmentally responsible, but they emphasize different levels of analysis and intervention. Off-site construction (OSC) research addresses the technological and process dimension of environmental sustainability, showing that prefabrication can reduce waste and carbon emissions while improving efficiency. It also identifies future needs such as comprehensive sustainability assessment, smart/computerized integration, circular-economy alignment, and region-specific evidence to strengthen adoption. (jayawardana2023environmentalsustainabilityof chunk 1)

The Ghana study shifts from technical potential to implementation constraints. It shows that sustainability in residential projects is hindered by four barrier clusters—management, standards, society, and knowledge—with management-related barriers being the most influential. This indicates that even when sustainability principles are known, organizational and institutional weaknesses can prevent effective uptake. (kineber2022identifyingandassessing chunk 1)

The Saudi “Mostadam” approach represents a formal framework for operationalizing sustainable residential buildings within Vision 2030. It provides a rating system tailored to Saudi social and privacy norms and aims to reduce energy use, improve building efficiency, and lower greenhouse-gas emissions. (balabel2021towardssustainableresidential chunk 1)

Across these contexts, the sustainability-related findings are consistent: environmental performance depends on both design/technology choices and enabling governance. Material selection, service life, and use-stage energy are critical hotspots in life-cycle terms; cleaner technologies such as solar PV, solar water heaters, and double glazing improve performance; and long service life helps only when components remain aligned to avoid maintenance burdens. (janjua2021sustainabilityimplicationsof chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-74ab432c: The excerpt explains that Saudi Arabia launched the “Mostadam” evaluation service to help both existing and new buildings meet sustainable building standards while respecting Saudi society’s privacy and principles. It is part of Vision 2030’s broader sustainable development agenda. The paper says Mostadam provides a conceptual framework and rating system for sustainable residential buildings, and it assesses the current state of sustainable buildings in Saudi cities. It highlights categories of sustainable residential buildings under Mostadam and explores their potential in Saudi Arabia, with the goal of reducing energy consumption, improving building efficiency, and lowering greenhouse-gas emissions.
From Ashraf Balabel and Mamdooh Alwetaishi. Towards sustainable residential buildings in saudi arabia according to the conceptual framework of “mostadam” rating system and vision 2030. Sustainability, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su13020793, doi:10.3390/su13020793.

pqac-c2e5900c: The excerpt identifies sustainability implementation barriers for residential building projects in Ghana. From prior studies and a questionnaire survey of Ghanaian construction firms, the barriers were grouped by exploratory factor analysis into four main categories: management, standards, society, and knowledge. Among these, management-related barriers were found by PLS-SEM to be the most significant in affecting sustainability implementation. The study focuses on sustainable residential buildings in Ghana and suggests these barriers are key obstacles to integrating green building principles into home construction projects.
From Ahmed Farouk Kineber, Ernest Kissi, and Mohammed Magdy Hamed. Identifying and assessing sustainability implementation barriers for residential building project: a case of ghana. Sustainability, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su142315606, doi:10.3390/su142315606.

pqac-76d2f3a6: The excerpt describes a 2023 systematic review on the environmental sustainability of off-site construction (OSC). It notes that OSC has been recognized for benefits including reduced construction time and cost, improved efficiency, and environmental savings. The abstract says OSC has proven advantages in environmental issues such as reduced waste generation and carbon emissions. The review compares developed and developing countries and identifies research gaps and future needs: comprehensive sustainability assessments, smart/computerized technology integration, prefabrication-rate research, circular economy and SDG integration, and region-specific studies. These findings are intended to help increase OSC adoption and improve environmental performance in building projects, including residential buildings.
From Janappriya Jayawardana, Asela K. Kulatunga, J. A. S. C. Jayasinghe, Malindu Sandanayake, and Guomin Zhang. Environmental sustainability of off-site construction in developed and developing regions: a systematic review. Journal of Architectural Engineering, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1061/jaeied.aeeng-1420, doi:10.1061/jaeied.aeeng-1420.

pqac-ceee29c7: The excerpt on Ghanaian residential building projects focuses on sustainability implementation barriers. It notes that sustainable construction should be integrated throughout development, but in developing contexts like Ghana limited resources make implementation difficult. A questionnaire survey of construction firms found four barrier categories from exploratory factor analysis: management, standards, society, and knowledge. Partial least squares SEM showed management-related barriers were the most significant impediments to sustainability implementation. The study emphasizes that removing these barriers can help policymakers improve cost savings, environmental performance, and social cohesion in residential buildings.
From Ahmed Farouk Kineber, Ernest Kissi, and Mohammed Magdy Hamed. Identifying and assessing sustainability implementation barriers for residential building project: a case of ghana. Sustainability, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su142315606, doi:10.3390/su142315606.

pqac-59bcb69d: The excerpt reports that sustainable residential building design should account for durability, affordability, resource conservation, and social equity over the full service life. Using a life cycle sustainability assessment (LCSA) framework, the study found that building sustainability depends strongly on material selection, service life, and component alignment. Case-study buildings with recycled steel-framed roofs, brick walls, and green concrete in slab footing performed better. The main sustainability hotspots were use-stage energy consumption and maintenance. Cleaner production strategies such as double-glazed windows, rooftop solar PV, and solar water heaters improved sustainability performance by 30–49%. Longer building life helps only if non-structural components last in alignment with the building to reduce maintenance impacts.
From Shahana Y. Janjua, Prabir Kumar Sarker, and Wahidul K. Biswas. Sustainability implications of service life on residential buildings – an application of life cycle sustainability assessment framework. Environmental and Sustainability Indicators, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.indic.2021.100109, doi:10.1016/j.indic.2021.100109.

contexts.context: The excerpt is about sustainable building renovation in Norwegian residential buildings. It frames retrofit as important for meeting Sustainable Development Goals and improving quality of life while reducing energy use and supporting affordable housing. A questionnaire of 341 citizens in Trondheim found that economic issues are the main barrier to SBR, with respondents calling for financial support. It also highlights social engagement with public/private partners and neighbors as a motivation, and suggests urban facility management as an intermediary to promote renovation in neighborhoods.

contexts.context: The excerpt is about coastal land reclamation in the Dammam Metropolitan Area, Saudi Arabia, and its environmental sustainability implications. Using satellite images from 2000–2020, the study found 6,081 hectares reclaimed from the Arabian Gulf through five major projects. It reports negative sustainability outcomes: degradation and loss of ecosystem services and marine habitat, increased urban sprawl, and higher flood risk. The authors argue that coastal reclamation disrupts marine environments and can undermine long-term sustainability due to rising water levels, earthquakes, and material behavior, and they recommend strict regulation and ecosystem-based urban planning. This relates to sustainability themes in built-environment research.

contexts.context: The excerpt is about a 2022 study assessing climate change impacts on urban sustainability in the Dammam Metropolitan Area, Saudi Arabia, using an expert survey (n=12) and Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). It finds the most significant climate change impacts are sea-level rise and coastal flooding, followed by threats to public health and low agricultural productivity, while groundwater depletion and urban heat islands are least impactful. For mitigation, experts ranked green infrastructure and sustainable transportation above green buildings, and the study recommends green infrastructure, sustainable transportation, and sustainable urban form as better options for climate mitigation and environmental sustainability in Saudi Arabia and similar regions.

session.formatted_answer:
Question: How do the themes of "Environmental sustainability", "Sustainability implementation barriers", and "Sustainable residential buildings" connect when comparing off-site construction research with the barrier analysis in Ghana and the "Mostadam" approach in Saudi Arabia, and what sustainability-related findings are highlighted across these contexts?

The three themes connect through a common focus on making residential construction more environmentally responsible, but they emphasize different levels of analysis and intervention. Off-site construction (OSC) research addresses the technological and process dimension of environmental sustainability, showing that prefabrication can reduce waste and carbon emissions while improving efficiency. It also identifies future needs such as comprehensive sustainability assessment, smart/computerized integration, circular-economy alignment, and region-specific evidence to strengthen adoption. (jayawardana2023environmentalsustainabilityof chunk 1)

The Ghana study shifts from technical potential to implementation constraints. It shows that sustainability in residential projects is hindered by four barrier clusters—management, standards, society, and knowledge—with management-related barriers being the most influential. This indicates that even when sustainability principles are known, organizational and institutional weaknesses can prevent effective uptake. (kineber2022identifyingandassessing chunk 1)

The Saudi “Mostadam” approach represents a formal framework for operationalizing sustainable residential buildings within Vision 2030. It provides a rating system tailored to Saudi social and privacy norms and aims to reduce energy use, improve building efficiency, and lower greenhouse-gas emissions. (balabel2021towardssustainableresidential chunk 1)

Across these contexts, the sustainability-related findings are consistent: environmental performance depends on both design/technology choices and enabling governance. Material selection, service life, and use-stage energy are critical hotspots in life-cycle terms; cleaner technologies such as solar PV, solar water heaters, and double glazing improve performance; and long service life helps only when components remain aligned to avoid maintenance burdens. (janjua2021sustainabilityimplicationsof chunk 1)
